### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/objectql`, touching **3** documentable anchor(s).

**6** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/data-modeling/objects.mdx`  _(via ObjectQLPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/kernel/services-checklist.mdx`  _(via ObjectQLPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/kernel/services.mdx`  _(via ObjectQLPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/permissions/authentication.mdx`  _(via ObjectQLPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/plugins/packages.mdx`  _(via ObjectQLPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/index.mdx`  _(via ObjectQLPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_

⛔ **2** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via ObjectQLPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-1.mdx`  _(via ObjectQLPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **58** of **210** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **20** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 7c3cc889f7c64d465486bb94ded8c8ea558d6945` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `66fb75a77b5ca348e83f7cae783d54e5607bad6a` — the merge of head `a2fb76a079fd8e6b022d4f9b86f263b2f3c1cbf1` into base `7c3cc889f7c64d465486bb94ded8c8ea558d6945`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 66fb75a77b5ca348e83f7cae783d54e5607bad6a && git checkout 66fb75a77b5ca348e83f7cae783d54e5607bad6a
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 7c3cc889f7c64d465486bb94ded8c8ea558d6945 a2fb76a079fd8e6b022d4f9b86f263b2f3c1cbf1 && git checkout -B drift-repro 7c3cc889f7c64d465486bb94ded8c8ea558d6945 && git merge --no-ff a2fb76a079fd8e6b022d4f9b86f263b2f3c1cbf1

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 7c3cc889f7c64d465486bb94ded8c8ea558d6945
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 7c3cc889f7c64d465486bb94ded8c8ea558d6945` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

Head-sha: `b4c76532970377a3e113509196fb60e13fd4d6bc`
Local-runs: none
Scope: `packages/objectql/src/plugin.ts`, `packages/objectql/src/manifest-service-residual-objects.test.ts`, `.changeset/28159-residual-picklist-unreferenced.md` + `packages/objectql/src/picklist-resolution.ts` (`collectManifestPicklistReferences`, `collectPicklistReferences`, `manifestSources`, `collectManifestPicklistNames`, `collectManifestPicklistExtensions`, `describeUnresolvedPicklistReferences`, `picklistMetadataError`), `packages/metadata/src/plugin.ts` (`unclaimedTopLevel`, `artifactItemSlot`, `ARTIFACT_FIELD_TO_TYPE`, `registerUnclaimedTopLevel`, the residual-rule header), `packages/objectql/src/registry.ts` (`findOrphanPicklistExtensions`), `packages/objectql/src/engine.ts` (the `picklistExtensions` branch of the body seam), `packages/runtime/src/app-plugin.ts` (the config door's `manifest.register` and `registerUnclaimedTopLevel` call sites), `packages/spec/src/stack.zod.ts` (`picklists`, the residual-rule prose at the permission-set owner gate, the `objectExtensions` target prose, the compose strategies), `packages/spec/src/data/field.zod.ts` (the `picklist` key and its type refinement), `packages/spec/src/ui/action.zod.ts` (param options), `packages/cli/src/utils/picklist-references.ts` (the author-time door's reading of a composed stack), `packages/objectql/CHANGELOG.md` (declaration precedent), `scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs`, `scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs`, `scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs`, `docs/adr/0130-release-artifact-as-co-ownership-boundary.md` D4.

Read-only: the tree was judged, not run.

Check-runs at 2026-10-30T18:54Z: 48 check-runs on the head, every one `completed`. 35 `success`, among them `Lint & Repo Gates`, `TypeScript Type Check`, `Build Core`, `Test Core` and all 8 shards, `Check Changeset`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `PR-body guards`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `Live E2E UI`, `Test UI`, every `Lint ·` and `Type Check ·` leg. 13 `skipped` are path-gated UI, docs and opt-in lanes. Nothing is still running. Since the merge-base, no commit on `origin/main` (now `7c3cc889`) touches `plugin.ts`, `picklist-resolution.ts`, `packages/metadata/src/plugin.ts` or the residual test file; the PR reads `mergeable_state: clean`.

### ① Derived judgments

Every accept-set and public-surface change the diff implies, judged in the tree:

1. **A composed stack whose residual holds a picklist that no object field names is refused at register, before anything of it registers** — right. `unreferencedResidualPicklistRefusal` reads the residual rule's own answer (`unclaimedTopLevel`, the one copy), takes its `picklist` entries by `name` (`artifactItemSlot` guarantees one), builds the "named" set from `collectManifestPicklistReferences` over the artifact and every body, and throws `picklistMetadataError` when any is left. The throw sits after the three residual reads and before the `packages: []` branch, both sealed audits and the `registerApp` loop, so a refused artifact registers nothing (pinned after `start()`: owners and package ids unchanged). The error is the existing envelope: `INVALID_METADATA`, 422, `httpStatus` 422; no new code.
2. **The refusal is judged off the artifact alone, never the registry** — right, and the right choice: the registry is still filling during a boot (the same reason `registerUnclaimedTopLevelObjects` judges off the bodies). "Named" means a `picklist` key on a field (`collectPicklistReferences`), in either field spelling, on `objects` and `objectExtensions`, in the manifest and its nested `plugins[]`. The field schema admits the `picklist` key on option types only (`field.zod.ts` refinement) and no other published surface names a picklist item by name (actions' params carry inline options; dashboards and kanban lanes read a field's picklist through the field), so the field key is the whole reference surface. But see ④ should-fix #1: the artifact's TOP LEVEL contributes references from items the engine never registers.
3. **A residual picklist that a field names keeps the #28093 line** — right. A residual object's field naming it: `registerUnclaimedTopLevelObjects` still lists that object and does not serve it (one warning), the list stays unregistered (pinned, the CONTROL that was already red under ablation A2). A body object's field naming it: `named` holds it, so this refusal is silent; the `kernel:ready` audit (`findUnresolvedPicklistReferences`) refuses it as "no loaded package declares" (pinned, the wording asserted). The residual objects rule's line does not move.
4. **A picklist a body declares is never residual** — right: `unclaimedTopLevel` claims every slot a body occupies, so a top-level copy (the ADR-0130 D4 read-both shape, or `composeStacks`' `picklists: 'concat'`) is claimed by name and never reaches this refusal (pinned both ways).
5. **A stack without `packages[]` is untouched** — right: `unclaimedTopLevel` answers `undefined` without an array `packages`, and its top-level picklists register through `registerApp` as before (pinned: the unnamed list resolves to `['a']`).
6. **`packages: []` with only such a picklist is refused** — right: with no body nothing is claimed, so every top-level item is residual under `manifest.id`; the refusal fires before the "registered nothing" warning (pinned).
7. **Both boot doors meet the refusal** — right. The config door (`AppPlugin.init`) hands the whole stack to `manifest.register` before its own `registerUnclaimedTopLevel`; the refusal propagates out of `init` and the boot fails. The late paths (install, rehydrate) enter the same `register` and are refused before the sealed picklist audit, which on `main` would already have refused a body's `picklistExtensions` entry extending the residual list as an orphan (③).
8. **No public export, route, schema or spec surface changes.** `packages/spec` is untouched; the only published package the diff moves is `@objectstack/objectql`.

### ② Semver level

- Changeset `.changeset/28159-residual-picklist-unreferenced.md`: `@objectstack/objectql` `patch`; body carries `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: none`, both line-initial and identical to the PR body's two lines.
- `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` is right for the arm: a composition that booted on `main` (①.1, ①.6) is refused on the head; nothing is widened. The title carries `!` and the body a **BREAKING** banner scoped to composed stacks, as a declared narrowing owes.
- `Metadata-protocol: none` is right: no key, accepted value, type or default an author writes changes; `PicklistSchema` and `ObjectStackDefinitionSchema` accept what they accepted, and the refusal is a composition-time judgement of the same class as the boot's existing picklist audit. `check-changeset-no-major.mjs` states the rule the other way too (a `(narrowing)` arm never becomes `narrowed`), and this package has shipped the same pair for boot-time refusals before (`504d8b3`, the `controlled_by_parent` boot refusal; `be78977`). Level per ruling A: `none` takes `patch`. Right; `Check Changeset` green.
- ADR-0087 marker `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`: right. No metadata surface is retired, so `objectstack migrate meta` has nothing to rewrite; the changeset's "remedy" is an authoring choice among three placements of a declaration, not a FROM-to-TO rewrite of consumer code, and the gate that re-checks that claim statement-against-statement is green on the head.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions: []` in the os-dev report — none to answer.
- Dev finding (carrier: seat, not filed): **a residual picklist that a body's `picklistExtensions` entry extends but no field names is now refused here, not by the orphan-extension audit.** Read and answered: on `main` the residual list is never in the engine registry, so `findOrphanPicklistExtensions` reports the extension at `kernel:ready` and the boot fails with the audit's envelope; on a late artifact the sealed audit's orphan leg refuses it at register. On the head the new refusal fires first with its own words. Refused on both trees, so no narrowing beyond the one declared; the new message's first remedy (declare the list inside the `packages[]` entry of the package whose objects use it) is also the right fix for an extension. The dev is right that nothing pins it — **should-fix #2** below.
- Dev's instruction-conflict note (assignee): AGENTS.md governs; no action here.
- Dev's deviations note (suites run outside `os-verify-lock`, the relay timeout on `pr_create`): the PR was confirmed once by REST read and nothing was re-sent; the check-runs on the head are the gate verdicts this record relies on, not the local figures.
- Context: #28093's should-fix #3 named exactly this card; record 6526074825 carried it as "filed as #28159, nothing further owed on #28153". The head takes triage's second option (refuse loudly with a prescription) and leaves the objects rule's line where the triage said it stays; the triage's conditional ("if registering is cleaner, state the moved line") was not taken, and the PR says so.
- Governed surfaces: none in the file list (`Governed Surface Queue Guard` green). `engine.ts` and `packages/spec` untouched, as the claim required.
- **Out of scope, found while reading, carried as should-fix #3:** the author-time door (`os compile` / `os validate`, `packages/cli/src/utils/picklist-references.ts`) reads a composed stack's picklists as its bodies' alone ("NOT the top level, which the load path does not register from") and so never looks at a top-level picklist in a composed stack: an author learns of this refusal only at boot. The published spec's prose at the permission-set owner gate (`stack.zod.ts`, "a top-level set that no body declares is the stack's residual, registered under `manifest.id`") states the residual rule with no picklist exception, while the head's own docblock (`RESIDUAL_TYPES_WITH_OWN_PATH`) now carries one. Both surfaces are outside this claim's file surface.

### ④ Design judgment

**The narrowing itself, against the published spec on `main`.** The spec declares `picklists` as "shared option lists that select fields reference by name", admits the `picklist` key on option-typed fields only, and reads a composed stack's picklist vocabulary as its bodies' at every door that judges a reference: `os compile` resolves a body's field against the bodies' lists alone and refuses otherwise; the boot's `kernel:ready` audit refuses a body's field naming a list only the top level declares; the residual objects rule lists and does not serve a residual object whose field names one. So on `main` a top-level picklist of a composed stack has no field it can serve, by every judge the platform already runs; the one case where nothing said anything was the list no field names, which the metadata door listed under `manifest.id` and the engine never held. Does the head take a declared capability away at the consumer? The capability the spec declares for a picklist (be offered by a field) was never deliverable from a composed stack's top level, and that is already the ruled line of #28093, pinned and unchanged here. What the head removes is a listing with nothing behind it, and it replaces silence with the refusal the sibling judges already give the referenced case, with the three remedies. That is making the platform's own refusal real for the one gap, not narrowing a delivered capability. The route is triage's, and the PR declares it as a narrowing, which is the honest arm. Holds, with the spec-prose and author-time gap named in should-fix #3 so the published spec says the line the runtime now enforces.

**`packages/objectql/src/plugin.ts`** — holds, with one should-fix. Break attempts:
- *A reference the check could miss.* Lookup, formula, master-detail and text fields carry no `picklist` key by schema; a `picklist` key on a non-option type is refused at parse, and at runtime `collectPicklistReferences` reads the key off any field regardless of type, so the runtime set is a superset of what strict parsing admits. Views, actions, reports and dashboards never name a picklist item. `objectExtensions` in a body and nested `plugins[]` are walked. No miss found.
- *A reference the check counts that never registers* — **should-fix #1.** `collectManifestPicklistReferences(artifact, undefined)` walks the artifact's whole top level: every top-level `objects` entry, including the copies a body claims (which the residual rule never registers from the top level) and the top-level `objectExtensions`, which in a composed stack no door registers (`RESIDUAL_TYPES_WITH_OWN_PATH`'s own words: the residual rule never lists one; `stack.zod.ts`: "the top-level `objectExtensions` are not read there"), and the top-level `plugins[]`, which only a body's `registerApp` registers. A residual picklist named ONLY by one of those is held as "named", not refused, and is then dropped exactly as the card describes, while nothing serves the field either. Reachable through a top-level `objectExtensions` entry in a composed stack (itself silently dropped on `main`, a separate defect) or a top-level object copy whose fields diverge from the body's. Fix: build `named` from the bodies plus the residual's own `object` entries (`residual.items.filter(type === 'object')`), which is the set `registerUnclaimedTopLevelObjects` judges, and pin the top-level-`objectExtensions` case red. Not a must-fix: the hole is narrower than the one the head closes, and nothing that booted on `main` is wrongly refused by it.
- *The referenced residual case moving by accident.* The CONTROL pins hold both sides (residual object's field: listed and not served, list unregistered; body object's field: the audit's words, not this refusal's). Holds.
- *Late artifacts.* The refusal precedes the sealed audits; a late artifact's residual picklist that a body field names is refused by the sealed audit's unresolved leg (declared is the bodies' names, the registry does not hold it), the same answer the boot gives. Holds.
- *Order and partial state.* Thrown before `registerApp`, before the residual registrations and before the bridge; the config door's metadata-side `registerUnclaimedTopLevel` runs after `manifest.register` in `init`, so a refused boot writes nothing there either. Holds.
- *Owner fallback.* With no `manifest.id` and no `id` the message names the stack by the literal none fallback, the spelling the objects rule's warning uses. Holds.
- *The envelope.* `picklistMetadataError` is the audit's; `PicklistMetadataError` is imported as a type for the return. Holds.
- *Docblocks.* The `RESIDUAL_TYPES_WITH_OWN_PATH` entry now states the refusal; the new function's docblock states the artifact-only judgement. Right, apart from should-fix #1's precision.

**`packages/objectql/src/manifest-service-residual-objects.test.ts`** — holds. Nine pins in one `describe`: the refusal's code, status, picklist, stack and all three remedies; several lists in one refusal and the named one excluded; `packages: []`; post-`start()` refusal with nothing registered; and five CONTROLs that hold the four unchanged lines (residual-field, body-field, body-declared with and without a top-level copy, no residual picklist, no `packages[]`). Fixtures reuse the file's `residualStack` / `payload` shape, the one `AppPlugin` hands over. Nothing pins the `picklistExtensions` case (should-fix #2) or the top-level-`objectExtensions` case (should-fix #1).

**`.changeset/28159-residual-picklist-unreferenced.md`** — holds (②): level, both declaration lines, the BREAKING banner scoped to composed stacks, the ADR-0087 marker and the remedy match the diff.

**Should-fixes:**
1. `unreferencedResidualPicklistRefusal` counts references from top-level items the engine never registers (`objectExtensions`, body-claimed object copies, top-level `plugins[]`); judge "named" off the bodies plus the residual's own objects, and pin the top-level-`objectExtensions` case.
2. Pin the case the dev flagged: a body's `picklistExtensions` entry extending a residual picklist that no field names is refused by this refusal, at boot and after `start()`.
3. File the follow-up card (outside this claim's surface): the author-time door (`packages/cli/src/utils/picklist-references.ts`) should report a composed stack's top-level picklist that no body declares and no field names, so `os validate` foretells this boot refusal; and the published spec's residual-rule prose (`packages/spec/src/stack.zod.ts`, the permission-set owner gate's docblock; the residual-rule header in `packages/metadata/src/plugin.ts`) should carry the picklist line the runtime now enforces (referenced: listed and not served; unreferenced: refused).

No must-fix. No fail-open finding at rule level beyond the one the card names and the head closes.

The PR reads `mergeable_state: clean`, still a draft.

### ① Derived judgments

The merge, judged by the tree:
1. **`a2fb76a0` is a plain merge.** Its tree is byte-identical to the automatic merge of its two parents (`942aae2b` and `7c3cc889`, the `origin/main` it took in); nothing was resolved by hand. The two `main` commits it brings (`3739d8d6`, `7c3cc889`) touch spec and lint surfaces only, none of the cited files. The net `plugin.ts` and test-file deltas against `main` differ from the first record's by exactly the fix commit's lines (interdiff read); the net file list is still the same three files. The first record's ①.1, ①.3–①.8 stand unchanged.

The fix, judged by the tree (`unreferencedResidualPicklistRefusal`):
2. **"Named" is now judged off the fields the engine registers from this artifact, and nothing else** — right, and it is the first record's should-fix #1 taken in full. The `artifact` parameter is gone; the sources are `[...bodies, { objects: residualObjects }]`, where `residualObjects` are the residual rule's own `object` entries — the set `registerUnclaimedTopLevelObjects` registers. `collectManifestPicklistReferences` over a body still walks its `objects`, its `objectExtensions` and its nested `plugins[]` (`manifestSources`), each of which `registerApp` registers; over the synthetic `{ objects }` it walks the residual's objects alone, and that object has no `objectExtensions` or `plugins` key to widen it.
